prompt: A sportswear brand is deciding whether to launch a line of smart running shoes with built-in sensors. The candidate's framework: (1) Runner demand for sensor-equipped shoes; (2) Price runners would pay; (3) Manufacturing and sensor costs; (4) Customer interest in smart running gear. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Missing: sensor costs for each pair
options.feedback: Sensor costs are in bucket 3, manufacturing and sensor costs.

options.text: Buckets 1 and 4 overlap: interest in smart gear is demand
options.feedback: Right. Customer interest in smart running gear is the same question as runner demand. Replace bucket 4 with competition from watches and fitness trackers.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: sensor costs will fall quickly
options.feedback: Even falling costs decide whether the shoes make money at launch, so bucket 3 belongs.

options.text: It's a generic launch framework: it ignores what makes sensor shoes different
options.feedback: The buckets are specific to sensor shoes: sensor costs and demand for sensor-equipped shoes. The flaw is that buckets 1 and 4 repeat each other.

explanation: Demand and customer interest are the same question. Better: demand, pricing, costs, competition from wearables, and the brand's ability to build electronics.

extras.corrected_framework: Demand; pricing; costs; competition (watches, trackers); capabilities in electronics
